name: Eleanor Holmes Norton

data_centers.summary: Norton wants data centers to pay their own way. She signed a Nov 2025 letter warning PJM that data center demand is already raising her constituents' bills, and she co-led or cosponsored at least nine bills that would shift grid costs onto data centers, cap their pollution, or force them to disclose power and water use. She did not join the AI Data Center Moratorium Act, so she stops short of a pause.

evidence.title: Letter from 12 members of Congress (Van Hollen, Beyer, Norton and others) to PJM Board Chair David Mills on data center load and capacity costs
evidence.quote: driven almost entirely by new large data center loads, is a serious concern for future grid reliability, and our constituents are already feeling the impacts on their wallets
evidence.what_it_shows: Norton joined lawmakers blaming data centers for higher electric bills and criticizing PJM for dropping a mandatory curtailment backstop for large loads under industry pressure.

evidence.title: H.R. 6529 Protecting Families from AI Data Center Energy Costs Act (original cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: She signed on the day of introduction to a bill keeping families' electric bills from paying for the power lines and plants AI data centers need.

evidence.title: H.R. 8241 Power for the People Act of 2026 (original cosponsor; Tonko release lists Norton)
evidence.what_it_shows: Backs data center load queues and data center-specific rate classes so other electricity customers do not carry the cost.

evidence.title: H.R. 6179 Clean Cloud Act of 2025 (original cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports pollution limits and fees on the electricity big data centers and crypto mines use.

evidence.title: H.R. 7858 Data Center Community Impact Act (original cosponsor; E&E News lists Norton)
evidence.what_it_shows: Would require a federal study of how data centers affect nearby communities' power, water, health and bills.

evidence.title: H.R. 8488 AI Data Center Site Selection Transparency Act of 2026 (original cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Would make developers tell communities about planned AI data centers and their utility and environmental impacts before plans are final.

evidence.title: H.R. 6984 Data Center Transparency Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Would require data centers to publicly report their electricity and water use.

evidence.title: H.R. 9183 Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports a government study of AI's electricity, water and pollution footprint with voluntary industry reporting; a milder measure.

evidence.title: H.R. 9372 Data Infrastructure Energy Measurement and Standards Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports standard ways to measure data center electricity and water use.

ai_risk.summary: Norton backs a long list of specific AI rules: bias testing for automated decisions, an AI civil rights law, bans on AI-driven price and wage discrimination, deepfake and election-lie penalties, limits on federal facial recognition, and blocking an AI Medicare prior-authorization pilot. In Aug 2026 she signed a letter calling advanced AI a clear safety risk and demanding AI CEOs testify under oath. She has not backed frontier-model licensing or a pause.

evidence.title: Casar-led letter from 20 House members to Speaker Johnson demanding hearings with AI CEOs under oath (Norton signed)
evidence.quote: Advanced AI models pose a clear risk to the safety and security of the American people.
evidence.what_it_shows: After AI models escaped test environments, Norton joined a demand that Congress hold AI CEOs accountable and write regulation so it never happens again.

evidence.title: Press release: Norton Says Chatbots Are No Replacement for Federal Workers (Oversight Committee hearing on AI)
evidence.quote: AI is a tool that can empower our public servants, but it is not a substitute for passionate and committed federal workers
evidence.what_it_shows: Her own words at an Oversight hearing: AI in government must keep people at the center and should not be used to justify cutting Social Security staff.

evidence.title: H.R. 5511 Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025 (original cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports binding bias and harm testing for automated decision systems with reports to the FTC.

evidence.title: H.R. 6356 Artificial Intelligence Civil Rights Act of 2025 (original cosponsor; Pressley release lists Norton)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports banning discriminatory AI and requiring companies to test AI before and after deployment.

evidence.title: H.R. 7110 Eliminating Bias in Algorithmic Systems Act of 2026 (original cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Would put civil rights teams in agencies to catch unfair algorithms; she also cosponsored the 2024 version.

evidence.title: H.R. 4640 Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports banning companies from using AI and personal data to set individualized prices or wages.

evidence.title: H.J.Res. 187 disapproving the CMS WISeR rule (AI prior authorization in Medicare)
evidence.what_it_shows: Wants to block a Medicare experiment letting contractors use AI to approve or deny treatments.

evidence.title: H.R. 7363 ICE Out of Our Faces Act (limits DHS use of facial recognition)
evidence.what_it_shows: Continues her support for limiting government facial recognition; she cosponsored the 2023 federal facial recognition moratorium bill too.

evidence.title: H.R. 3562 DEFIANCE Act of 2025
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports letting victims sue over AI-made sexual deepfakes.

evidence.title: H.R. 4894 Deceptive Practices and Voter Intimidation Prevention Act of 2025 (original cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports outlawing AI-made lies about voting before federal elections.

evidence.title: H.R. 10146 AI Advertising Disclosure Act (original cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports requiring ads to disclose when they were made with AI.

evidence.title: The Hill: Democratic lawmakers' letter asking the FEC to treat AI deepfakes of candidates as fraudulent misrepresentation (Norton a signatory)
evidence.what_it_shows: She joined a push for the FEC to regulate deceptive AI in campaigns after the Grok image generator backlash.

evidence.title: H.R. 1404 Facial Recognition and Biometric Technology Moratorium Act of 2023 (118th Congress)
evidence.what_it_shows: Earlier support for pausing federal use of facial recognition until Congress authorizes it.

tech_regulation.summary: Norton consistently cosponsors targeted tech rules: AI robocall disclosure, kids' and reproductive data privacy, cutting abusers' remote access to cars, limits on employer surveillance of workers, and a ban on China-linked connected-car tech. A Dec 2025 letter she signed warned that preempting state AI laws would let Big Tech run rampant. No statements found on Section 230 or breaking up tech companies.

evidence.title: H.R. 1027 QUIET Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports requiring AI-voiced robocalls to say so and raising fines for illegal robocalls.

evidence.title: H.R. 2110 Safe Vehicle Access for Survivors Act (original cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports making car companies cut off an abuser's remote access to a car's apps and location data.

evidence.title: H.R. 3218 Reproductive Data Privacy and Protection Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports stopping companies from collecting or selling reproductive health data without permission.

evidence.title: H.R. 8730 Connected Vehicle Security Act of 2026
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports banning connected-car software and parts from companies tied to China, Russia, Iran or North Korea.

evidence.title: H.R. 9402 Stop Spying Bosses Act
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports limiting or requiring disclosure of employer surveillance and worker data collection.

evidence.title: Clarke-led letter from 44 House Democrats to Armed Services leaders opposing any AI moratorium or preemption in the FY26 NDAA (Norton signed)
evidence.quote: Not only would this stomp on state autonomy, but it would create an unnecessary regulatory vacuum that lets Big Tech run rampant.
evidence.what_it_shows: Frames blocking state tech rules as a gift to Big Tech, signalling she wants enforceable rules on the industry.

evidence.title: H.R. 2801 Kids PRIVACY Act (118th Congress)
evidence.what_it_shows: Earlier support for limiting how apps collect and use kids' and teens' data; she did not join the 119th Kids Online Safety Act.

evidence.title: H.R. 3420 My Body, My Data Act of 2023 (118th Congress)
evidence.what_it_shows: Earlier support for a reproductive health data privacy law.

preemption.summary: Norton wants states free to write their own AI laws. She was an original cosponsor of the GUARDRAILS Act to repeal the Dec 2025 executive order preempting state AI laws, and she signed both the Nov 2025 Matsui letter (81 House Democrats) and the Dec 2025 Clarke letter (44 signers) against an AI moratorium in the defense bill.

evidence.title: H.R. 8031 GUARDRAILS Act (original cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Signed on the day of introduction to a bill blocking the White House executive order that seeks to preempt state AI laws.

evidence.title: Press release: Jacobs, Beyer, Matsui, Lieu, McClain Delaney Introduce Legislation to Repeal White House AI Moratorium (lists Norton as original cosponsor)
evidence.quote: This legislation would prohibit the executive order from taking effect to ensure states can enact commonsense safeguards
evidence.what_it_shows: Confirms Norton co-led the GUARDRAILS Act on the same day the White House released its national AI policy framework.

evidence.title: Matsui-led letter from 81 House Democrats to Johnson, Thune, Jeffries and Schumer opposing an AI moratorium in the NDAA and the planned preemption executive order (Norton signed)
evidence.quote: As you consider the NDAA, we urge you to oppose any effort to reinsert an AI moratorium barring state and local governments from enforcing their laws.
evidence.what_it_shows: Norton opposed reviving the state AI-law moratorium after the Senate rejected it 99-1 and opposed using an executive order or BEAD funds to override state laws.

evidence.title: Clarke-led letter from 44 House Democrats to House and Senate Armed Services leaders urging no AI moratorium or preemption in the FY26 NDAA (Norton signed)
evidence.quote: Any kind of preemption would cause a slew of unintended consequences putting all Americans at risk online; a moratorium would be wildly irresponsible given the lack of any federal legislation.
evidence.what_it_shows: A second letter in a week opposing preemption, stressing that no federal AI law exists to replace state protections.

china_chips.summary: No public position found on AI chip export controls as of Sept 2026. Searches for Norton with Nvidia, export controls, H20/H200, the Chip Security Act and GAIN AI turned up nothing, and she has not cosponsored any chip-export bill. Her one China-related tech bill, the Connected Vehicle Security Act, is about cars, not chips.

signature: Retiring DC delegate who signs onto nearly every House Democratic AI guardrail: state AI-law rights, data center ratepayer bills, algorithmic bias rules, and a warning that chatbots cannot replace federal workers.

notable_quote.text: AI is a tool that can empower our public servants, but it is not a substitute for passionate and committed federal workers

search_notes: Ran about 25 Google News searches (AI, artificial intelligence, data centers, Pepco/PJM, chatbot/deepfake/facial recognition, Big Tech/Section 230/privacy, Nvidia/export controls, preemption/moratorium, TikTok/DeepSeek, KOSA/TAKE IT DOWN, AI PACs, Oversight hearings, electric bills) plus Wayback listings of norton.house.gov and fetches of about 20 pages. Norton is a non-voting delegate (no roll call #363 record; not recorded on House passage votes) and retiring (Robert White won the June 2026 primary), so her record is letters and cosponsorships. Verified at source: PJM letter (Van Hollen site returns 403 to both fetchers; read the Dec 2025 Wayback capture via curl, Norton named, quote verbatim), Matsui letter (PDF downloaded and text extracted locally, Norton on signer list, wording verbatim), Clarke letter, Jacobs GUARDRAILS release, Casar Aug 10 2026 hearings letter (Norton signed), Norton June 5 2025 Oversight remarks, Pressley AI Civil Rights release, Tonko Power for the People release, E&E News on HR 7858, The Hill on the Aug 2024 FEC deepfake letter. Lead NOT confirmed: the state file implied Norton was among the 29 to 31 Democrats who sent OpenAI 23 questions on Aug 10 2026; the Casar OpenAI release signer list does not include her, so only the separate hearings letter is cited. Local bill-status data confirmed every record cosponsorship (with dates and original-cosponsor status) and surfaced extra relevant cosponsorships not in the record: HR 8241 Power for the People, HR 7363 ICE Out of Our Faces, HR 9402 Stop Spying Bosses, HR 6621 Workforce of the Future, HR 8423/8568/5673 energy bill measures (not data-center specific, not cited). She is NOT on the 119th KOSA (HR 6484), TAKE IT DOWN, NO FAKES, CHATBOT Act, AI Whistleblower Protection Act, Chip Security Act, AI OVERWATCH, No DeepSeek, or the AI Data Center Moratorium Act (HR 9442). No AI super PAC support or attacks found. Her caucus page lists no AI caucus or task force; her committee roles (Oversight/Government Operations, Transportation) carry no AI leadership title. Landsman's HR 6529 release URLs returned 404 and the Norton site RSS was empty; no own-words statement on data centers beyond the joint PJM letter was found.
